items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1861

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the administrative code of the city of New York and
the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to increasing the fine for
commercial vehicles that park on residential streets overnight


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This legislation raises the parking fines for commercial vehicles
parked in New York City residential zones and provides for the
placement of signs regarding such fines.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section 1. Amends subdivision c of section 19-170 of chapter 5 of
title 19 of the administrative code of the city of New York, raising
the fine for commercial vehicles parked overnight on New York City
residential streets to $750 for a first offense and $1250 for each
subsequent offense within a six-month period.
Section 2. Directs the Department of Transportation to place signs in
affected areas informing the general public about these fines.
Section 3. Sets the effective date of 60 days after becoming a law.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The current fine for parking a commercial vehicle on a New York City
residential street between 9pm and 5am is $50. This sum is
inconsequential when compared to the costs of storing such vehicles in
off street parking, leaving many commercial vehicle owners to choose
illegal parking on streets over other options. As a result, city
residents find precious parking spaces occupied by illegally parked
commercial vehicles. This legislation seeks to alleviate this problem
and ensure violators are properly informed of the fines via signs in
affected areas.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2008 - S.6544A - Referred to Cities

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Increase in revenue from parking fines; cost of placement of signs by
Department of Transportation

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Sixty days after becoming law.

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S1861C

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the administrative code of the city of New York and the
vehicle and traffic law, in relation to
increasing the fine for tractor-trailer combinations
that park on residential streets overnight

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
This legislation raises the parking fines
for tractor-trailer combinations, large tractors,
truck-trailers, and semi-trailers that are parked in New York city
residential zones.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Section 1. Amends subdivision c of section 19-170 of chapter 5 of
title 19 of the administrative code of the city of New York, to raise
the fine for tractor-trailer combinations, tractors, truck-trailers,
and semi-trailers that park overnight on New York City residential
streets to $250 for a first offense and $500 for each subsequent
offense within a six-month period.

Section 2. Amends Vehicle & Traffic Law section 237(2) to authorize
the City of New York to impose the traffic penalties provided for in
section 1 of this bill.

JUSTIFICATION:
The current fine for parking a commercial vehicle on a
New York city residential street between 9pm and 5am is $50. This
small sum of money is of little deterrent value when compared to the
costs of parking such vehicles in off-street parking sites. The
current situation encourages many commercial vehicle owners to choose
to illegally park their large truck-cabs and trailers on city streets
over other less costly options. As a result, city residents find
precious parking spaces occupied by illegally parked tractor-trailer
combinations. This legislation seeks to alleviate this problem.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
2008 - S.6544A - Referred to Cities

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Increase in revenue from parking fines.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
Sixty days after it shall have become law.
